synthesizedApproach:
## Three things need Tim before IMPLEMENT

**1. The sink's destination leaks the exact cause to the agent on any denied call.** Verified: `Program.RunHookAsync` writes `execution.Message` and its fail-closed text to **stderr** and returns exit 2 (`src/AgentGuard.Cli/Program.cs:187-201`); Claude Code feeds a hook's stderr to the model on exit 2. So if group 3's exact grant/key causes go to a stderr sink, and that same call then denies — which is the normal case, since a rejected grant is why it denies — the agent reads the exact cause. The unit test for acceptance 8a would still pass while decision `tell` is broken in production. The carrier (`Loaded<T>.Why`) is approved; the destination is not settled by any approved principle. Options: a file under the existing machine directory (my recommendation, but writing to the user's machine is best-practices 4b and therefore his), buffer and flush the sink only on an allow (a new mechanism, not approved), or accept stderr and accept the leak on a deny. Do not default this.

**2. The two build-only release legs.** The contract permits either branch ("run the tests they build, or record in `docs/silent-failure-audit.md` why a leg stays build-only"), and the design takes the recorded-reason branch because no x64-on-arm precedent exists for Windows or Linux in `ci.yml` and a new runner job outlives this work. But accepting a deferred check is best-practices 6b, which is his, so he should know it leaves two release RIDs never executed in CI and can overrule.

**3. Six analyzer/test rules against a contract that says "Rules to add: None."** They are listed in rulesToAdd. R1 (the comment-only / reason-dropping catch analyzer) is the one that must not be dropped: it is the mechanical guard for the exact defect class this whole issue is about, and acceptance check 9 is a one-shot Python regex that never runs again after this run. All six need him to edit the contract; scope changes only that way.

## Settled here, not sent to him

Three questions the candidates raised are already answered by the approved text, and bringing them to Tim would be bringing a settled answer as a decision.

- **The unreadable-link test seam on the doubles is already approved.** The contract says to "Update `ManagedPlatformFileSystem` and `InMemoryFileSystemStore` so a link marked unreadable in a test raises the same way, and add the fake state needed to mark one", and "What the agent MAY do" lists "Add test fakes and test state needed to exercise an unreadable link." symlink-and-catches asked for a yes it already has.
- **`ConditionState.Broken`, not `CannotVerify`.** symlink-and-catches argued Broken invites a repair that overwrites a link we could not read. Its own design removes that danger: `SymlinkOps.EnsurePointsTo` reads the link first (`SymlinkOps.cs:40`) and now raises before `MakeLinkTarget`, and `CreationHelper.RepairLink` (`CreationHelper.cs:232-244`) catches and returns `NotRepairable`. With the raise in place Broken cannot cause an overwrite, so the contract's approved wording stands and no contract edit is needed.
- **No narrow absent-path catch in `ReadLinkTarget`.** The contract says remove both catches; a `when (e is FileNotFoundException or DirectoryNotFoundException)` clause would pass acceptance 6's grep by construction, which is the rule-dodge shape the contract calls a wall. The probe is the existing spec test (`tests/AgentGuard.CrossPlatform.Tests/PlatformFileSystemSpecTests.cs:123-156`) running on the Windows CI leg. If it goes red there, that is a wall: stop and report, do not add a catch.

## Order of work

The sink first (group 4's product half), because group 3 reports through it. Then group 1, group 3, group 2, group 5. One piece, one adversary round (decision `scope`).

## Group 4 — the warning sink (the spine)

`IWarningSink` in `src/AgentGuard.Abstractions/Contracts` with one member, `void Warn(string message)`, exposed as `ISystemServices.Warnings`. The shape mirrors `IConsole` (`void`, string in — `IConsole.ErrorWriteLine` is the same shape), per best-practices 2c layer 3. Records and interfaces are legal in Abstractions (`NoClassInAbstractionsAnalyzer` bans only a public plain class; `public sealed record CaptureFailed(string Reason)` is the precedent at `CaptureFailed.cs:10`).

**Who owns the stderr write.** Verified constraint that no candidate fully resolved: AG0031 reports any ordinary method taking a lone owned service, exempting only `Program` in the CLI and the test `SystemServicesBuilder` (`NoServiceAsParameterAnalyzer.cs:70-88`, `CompositionPoint.cs:60-63`). `SystemServices.Create` in Engine is **not** exempt, so `WarningSinkAdapter.Create(IConsole console)` called from there is a diagnostic. Once `IWarningSink` is on the container it is itself an owned interface, so handing it into any `Create(...)` is the same diagnostic. The clean shape is therefore to reuse the existing owner of stderr: `ConsoleAdapter` in `AgentGuard.Boundaries` also implements `IWarningSink`, reached through a parameterless factory on that owner, and the instance is handed to the `SystemServices` constructor (constructor parameters are exempt). If `container-interface-single-owner` or AG0005 refuses one class owning two container interfaces, that is a wall: stop and report, never suppress and never reshape.

The adapter writes one line through the owned console, matching the existing prefix shape at `Program.cs:200` (`agentguard: failing closed — …`). Exit code and verdict are untouched. If the write itself throws it propagates — the adapter does not swallow its own failure.

**Test container.** `SystemServicesBuilder` (`tests/AgentGuard.TestHelpers/SystemServicesBuilder.cs`, 14 existing slots) gets a `Slot<IWarningSink>`, a `With(IWarningSink)`, the `Wrap(...)` entry, and a recording fake; AG0019 fails the build otherwise. Write and RED-check the group 2 test before this change so a broken resolve is not mistaken for it (grafted from warning-sink).

**PrivilegedWriter** keeps the `foreach` and the bare `Task`: one `catch (Exception e) when (e is IOException or UnauthorizedAccessException)` per effect that warns, naming the effect kind, the path and `e.Message`, then continues; cancellation still propagates. Throwing would reach `RunPostAsync`'s catch-all and change a deny, which the contract forbids. It already takes `ISystemServices` (`PrivilegedWriter.cs:59`), so it adds `services.Warnings` with no new parameter.

**Pipeline** already holds `_services` (`Pipeline.cs:26,39`). `SweepBestEffortAsync` (174-188) and `DeleteBestEffortAsync` (190-204) are the same shape — a try around one store call with the same two catches — so they collapse into **one** private helper taking the store call and a one-line description, and that helper warns. The sweep still runs first and the call still proceeds; the delete still runs in `finally` after the verdict is chosen, which is exactly why a verdict cannot carry it.

**PosixFileSystem**: `TryRemoveLink` is deleted. The first call site (`:64`, pre-clearing a unique random temporary sibling) becomes a plain delete that propagates. The second (`:70`, immediately before the errno throw) folds the cleanup failure into that `IOException` as message text plus `InnerException`. The same edit reaches the Linux build through the csproj link; Windows has no `TryRemoveLink`. The contract's sentence "so the per-OS adapters are covered" is not literally true and is corrected in the record: they are covered by raising.

## Group 1 — the unreadable symlink

Delete both catches from `PlatformFileSystemBase.ReadLinkTarget` (`:41-48`). Null stays the answer for a non-link; `IsLinkTarget` inherits the raise. Update the `IPlatformFileSystem` docs at `:23-36` and the `MakeLinkTarget`/`RemoveLinkTarget` docs, and document on `IPathCanonicalizer.Canonicalize` that it raises for a cycle (already true, `PathCanonicalizer.cs:49-55`) and now for an unreadable link.

`PathCanonicalizer` gets no catch — it returns `CanonicalPath` and cannot carry a reason (decision `where`).

`FileGuard.PrecheckWriteAsync` gets the one catch that matters. Verified: `_canonicalizer.Canonicalize(rawPath)` at `FileGuard.cs:345` sits in a method with no catch, so today an unreadable link (and the existing cycle `IOException`) escapes Pre. One filter clause `when (e is IOException or UnauthorizedAccessException)` returning `Verdict.Deny($"Cannot canonicalize '{rawPath}', failing closed: {e.Message}")`. `Pipeline.RunPreAsync`'s catch-all (`Pipeline.cs:128-131`) already turns an escape into a deny, so this is not a second path to the same answer — it is the layer that names the specific thing, which best-practices 5b requires and the catch-all cannot do. The other callers need nothing: `CaptureAsync` already converts both exceptions into `CaptureFailed` carrying the message (`FileGuard.cs:90-100`), and the construction-time callers (`GuardEngine`, the matchers, `RegionMapRegistry`) abort startup loudly into `Program.cs:198-201`, which prints a named message and exits 2.

`SymlinkOps.EnsurePointsTo` is unchanged and now raises before `MakeLinkTarget`, ending the overwrite of an unreadable link. `CreationHelper.RepairLink` (`:232-244`) merges its existing `UnauthorizedAccessException` catch into one filter clause covering both types and returns `NotRepairable(e.Message)` — which also converts a failed-rename `IOException` from `MakeLinkTarget` into a not-repairable outcome instead of a crash; correct, and recorded.

`BinSymlinkCondition.DetectInstalled` and `CurrentSymlinkCondition.DetectInstalled` are byte-for-byte the same read-compare-report block with a different path, expected target and label (verified at `:20-33` in both). Fold the read, the catch and the compare into **one** shared helper, written once, returning `ConditionState.Broken($"… is an unreadable link: {e.Message}")`. That satisfies the contract's "must stop reporting an unreadable link as a link that points at ''".

`InstallIntegrity.HasCurrentEntry` (`:126-131`) gets no catch — an unreadable `current` is neither present nor absent, so it has no honest bool. The catch goes once at the integrity check's call site, returning `IntegrityReport.Deny("could not locate the install root; a `current` link is unreadable: …")`, reusing the pattern already at `InstallIntegrity.cs:85-97`. The per-OS link writers get no catch; a raise now stops them treating an unreadable link as a real entry.

## Group 3 — denials that lost the reason

Two channels, split at one seam (reason-carriers). The agent channel is the `Verdict` text; the trusted channel is the one sink from group 4, with `Loaded<T>(T Value, string? Why)` as the carrier Tim approved by name.

**Where `tell` binds and where it does not.** `tell` governs the grant/key path, where the rationale is the forgery oracle: `GrantStore` and `GuardEngine.LoadGrantPublicKey`. There the Deny text stays a fixed literal, chosen by whether `Why` is null, and never interpolates `Why`, an exception, or a path. `tell` does **not** rewrite the contract's explicit instruction for `FileGuard.TryReadCurrentAsync` (383-387), which says in terms that the message is carried into the Deny one frame up, and acceptance 5 asks for the same on the canonicalize path. reason-carriers overrode that; the override is rejected — scope changes only by Tim editing the contract.

Carry this to him as a reported finding, not a fix: `Pipeline.cs:119` already renders `CaptureFailed.Reason` into `Verdict.Deny($"Capture failed, failing closed: {failed.Reason}")`, `ClaudeCodeHostAdapter.Render` puts that straight into `HostDecision` (`:107-117`), and `FileGuard.cs:95,99,192,196,221,225` build those reasons from `exception.Message` and an absolute path. So raw exception text and absolute paths reach the agent today, outside the thirteen. Also tell him that acceptance 8a's "no absolute path" would fail against the pre-existing `{rawPath}` echo in the grant Deny unless the test is written against the added reason text; the path is the agent's own input, not an added leak.

`GrantStore.TryLoadAsync` stays private and returns `Loaded<Grant?>`: a fixed cause for an invalid signature and for an expiry, and `"<file>: <type>: <message>"` for each named exception. **Do not add an `UnauthorizedAccessException` catch there.** reason-carriers auto-resolved that as in-scope; it is not. Today it escapes to `Pipeline.RunPreAsync`'s catch-all and becomes a hard Deny with the message, so it is neither silent nor reasonless — and catching it would let other grants still authorize the write, which changes whether the place denies and the contract forbids exactly that.

`IGrantStore.GetActiveGrantsAsync` returns `Task<Loaded<IReadOnlyList<Grant>>>` (approved by name in decision `loaded`); update the XML doc and both production callers (`FileGuard.cs:236,355`). `GrantStore.Create` already takes `ISystemServices` (`GrantStore.cs:90-91`), so it reaches `services.Warnings` with no new parameter.

`GuardEngine.LoadGrantPublicKey` returns `Loaded<ReadOnlyMemory<byte>>`: absent file is `(Empty, "grant public key file not present: grants switched off")`; a key that exists and is corrupt, wrong-length or unreadable raises a trust-configuration failure with the exact cause and escapes to the composition root, where `Program.cs:200` prints it and exits 2 (decision `trust`).

`Ed25519SignatureService.Verify` keeps `bool` and never throws. It gets no sink: AG0031 forbids handing it one, and policy belongs at the call site, not in the boundary wrapper. Its two catches and the wrong-length early return name the exception in a comment and the cause is classified one layer up by `GrantStore.IsSignatureValid` (`GrantStore.cs:146-152`), the sole production caller of `Verify`. reason-carriers left this as a gap for Tim; it is closed here, so nothing goes to him.

`WindowsUserPresence` (`:154,175`) and `BuildOutputSkipRule` (`:47,51`) name their exception and report it to the sink, keeping their current result types. The presence detail is not added to `PresenceResult.Detail`, which is shown at the prompt boundary.

## Group 2 — the inert-fence test (adopted nearly whole from inert-fence-test)

One new `LiveContainerResolvesTests.cs` in `analyzers/AgentGuard.Analyzers.Tests` that compiles the **live source** of `src/AgentGuard.Abstractions` — not a project reference, because `AnalyzerRunner.ResolveReferencesAsync` resolves `ReferenceAssemblies.Net.Net90` (`AnalyzerRunner.cs:150`) while `Directory.Build.props:13` sets `net10.0`, and because a new project reference is a new dependency edge this work does not need. Three facts, all failing loudly with a message naming `ISystemServices`, the live path and the seven analyzers: (1) `ResolveTree` over the live sources is non-null; (2) a bare consumer referencing those sources compiled as `AgentGuard.Abstractions` also resolves non-null, which is AG0034's referenced-assembly case; (3) `Resolve` and `ContainerInterfaces` over the live compilation equal the same over `SharedAnalyzerSources.RealShapeContainer`, which is the only thing that stops the hand copy drifting. Reuse `RepositoryFiles.FindRepositoryRoot()` (`:25`) and add a multi-source overload to `AnalyzerRunner` rather than copying `ResolveReferencesAsync`; keep `ThrowOnUnexpectedCompilerErrors` so an uncompilable live tree fails rather than skips. Enumerate `**/*.cs` excluding `obj` and `bin`, and assert the enumeration is non-empty so an empty folder fails instead of passing as nothing. Prove it red by pointing the helper at a folder without the type (acceptance 7).

## Group 5 — the pipeline (adopted from pipeline-and-tests)

`if-no-files-found: warn` → `error` at `ci.yml:127, 258, 381`, macOS included (same defect class). This forces a change to the existing `EvidenceUploadsCannotRegressTests`, whose conforming fixture carries `warn` and would pin the old value: extend `ConformanceProblems` to require `error` and move the fixture. That edits an existing test — tightening, not weakening — and still needs Tim's yes under the contract's MUST NOT list.

A local build keeps stamping `local` (decision `local`).

## Test-cleanup catches

The same `IOException` + `UnauthorizedAccessException` pair is written out in eight places. `TestTempDirectory.DeleteBestEffort` (`tests/Shared/TestTempDirectory.cs:24-37`) is the existing owner of temp-tree teardown: route `FixtureProject` and `CliMachine` to it and delete their copies rather than mirroring the catch. **The owner itself is one of the eight swallowers** — its two comment-only catches go, so a failed teardown surfaces; its doc ("Cleanup must never fail a test") is rewritten to say the opposite. `SetupHarness` deletes on the in-memory overlay where an `IOException` is a real bug, so its catch is removed. `PlatformFileSystemSpecTests.cs:302` replaces its `DirectoryNotFoundException` catch with an `Exists` check, so the benign case is a visible condition and anything else surfaces. Do not touch the stale copies under `.claude/worktrees`.

## Tests

Group 1: `ReadLinkTarget` null for non-link, absent and missing-parent (existing three stay); unreadable link raises the exact type on the double, plus an on-disk Windows case where an ACL can be arranged; Pre on a path crossing an unreadable link is a Deny carrying the message, not an uncaught exception and not Allow; `EnsurePointsTo` does not reach `MakeLinkTarget` and `RepairLink` returns `NotRepairable` for both exception types; the two conditions return `Broken` with the cause, never "points at ''"; integrity returns `Deny` with the reason; the per-OS writers raise instead of overwriting. Group 3: six assertions, one per place, that the exact cause reaches the sink (8); the agent-text assertions (8a, written against the added reason text); three `Verify` cases (8b); absent vs wrong-length key (8c); `Loaded<T>` carries both, and an expired grant and a corrupt key each give a non-empty reason (8d). Group 4: a store whose `SweepExpiredAsync` throws reaches the sink **and** the pipeline returns the same Pre verdict with a guard proven to have run (8e); first-of-three effect fails and the other two still run; two failures give two warnings; `OperationCanceledException` still propagates; a pointed-integration test that a failed temp cleanup appears in the thrown `IOException`. Every case named in the test output.

rulesToAdd.rule: No swallowing catch anywhere under src/ or tests/: a catch clause whose body is empty or contains only comments is an error, and so is a catch of IOException, UnauthorizedAccessException or Exception whose body neither rethrows, nor wraps the exception into one it throws, nor passes the exception variable (or its Message/ToString) into a value it returns, records, warns or asserts on. A legitimate exception is an ordinary [SuppressMessage] Tim approves, never a self-granted one.
rulesToAdd.failureModeStopped: The exact defect this whole issue exists to remove comes straight back the next time someone writes a best-effort cleanup or a teardown: a failure turned into null, false or nothing, so an unreadable thing reports as absent or fine and the guard acts on a wrong answer, or a product failure hides behind a green test. Verified gap: nothing in the tree catches this shape today — no analyzer, no .editorconfig entry, no S108/S2486 setting, and the CA1031 suppressions only cover sanctioned broad catches. Acceptance check 9 is a Python regex the worker runs once in its transcript and that never runs again.
rulesToAdd.analyzer: Roslyn syntax/semantic analyzer in analyzers/AgentGuard.Analyzers (new AG id), severity Warning-as-error like the rest of AgentGuard.Architecture, on CatchClauseSyntax: flag when the Block has no statements (trivia-aware, so a comment plus a real statement stays legal), or when the body has no ThrowStatement/ThrowExpression and the declared exception local is never read. It must be introduced AFTER the cleanup in this work, because on its first run it would light up every one of the sites being fixed.

rulesToAdd.rule: A Verdict reason string may not be built from a Loaded<T>.Why, from an exception, or from an exception's Message or ToString, anywhere a grant or key rejection is being reported. Only constants and the path the agent itself supplied may appear. The allow-list is the places the contract names as carrying a cause into a denial (the canonicalize catch in FileGuard.PrecheckWriteAsync and FileGuard.TryReadCurrentAsync's final Deny).
rulesToAdd.failureModeStopped: A later change copies the exact grant or key cause into the text the guarded agent reads, turning the denial into an oracle that separates an invalid signature from an expired grant from a wrong-length key — which is the forgery aid decision `tell` was taken to prevent — and leaking absolute paths with it. Today nothing but one test would notice, and the test can pass while the leak happens through a different frame.
rulesToAdd.analyzer: Roslyn operation analyzer on IInvocationOperation for Verdict.Deny/Warn/Block: walk the interpolated or concatenated reason argument and flag any operand whose type derives from System.Exception, any .Message/.ToString() on one, and any member access to Loaded<T>.Why.

Without this the fix is one text edit away from being undone.
rulesToAdd.analyzer: Contract-directed test rule (repository-file text test) extending the existing EvidenceUploadsCannotRegressTests and its step parser in analyzers/AgentGuard.Analyzers.Tests — extend the one owner, do not copy the parser.
